utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good afternoon to everybody. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-A, the Prosecutor versus Mladen Naletilic and Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I call for appearances. For the appellants.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Matt Hennessy, representing with Christopher Meek, Mladen Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am Zelimir Par, attorney from Sarajevo, and my colleague, Mr. Kurt Kerns is here with me, and together we are representing Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. May I turn to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution today is Norman Farrell, Mr. Steffen Wirth, and our case manager is Ms. Lourdes Galicia. During the Status Conference, Mr. Wirth will be addressing you on any issues, and if I can be of any assistance, I'll step in, but he's been working on the case while I've been on other matters this past week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. May I ask the appellants if they can hear me and follow the proceedings. I think it's the case. Thank you. Well, as you know, the purpose of the Status Conference is to first to allow any person in custody, as the appellants are, the opportunity to raise any issues in relation to their detention. Is there any concern of this kind to be raised in this Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Mr. Naletilic has asked to address the Court as to some matters, but as far as to the circumstances of his detention, no, he has no complaints, other than he is detained. But no, no problems with the manner of detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Any complaint as concerning the appellant Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no complaints. We spoke with our client today, and he doesn't have any questions that he would need to voice, so thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if there is no concern of this kind to be taken up, let me try to turn to the other aspect of the Status Conference, that is, to see where the appeal stands at this stage. I think the appellate filings have been completed now. As to the Prosecution appeal, the appeal brief is in. So are the responses of Mr. Naletilic and Martinovic, and we have a consolidated reply of the Prosecution. So I think as to that appeal all the briefs are in. The same applies to the appeal of Mr. Naletilic, where all the briefs have been filed, and the same applies as far as the appeal of Mr. Martinovic is concerned. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: As to Naletilic, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and also for Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. So now let's turn to pending issues. There is still, as far as the appeal -- or as far as Mr. Naletilic is concerned, there is pending a Rule 115 motion that the Appeals Chamber is considering and will deal with as soon as possible. I think this is the only pending motion, except for motions concerning protective measures. But if you want to deal with them, we should go into a private session, I guess, because there are -- it's a question of protected witnesses, actually. If the parties want to discuss this. If not, then we don't have to address them, and we don't have to go into private session. But perhaps -- please, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May it please the Court, I would like to go into private session for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Fine. Let's go into private session, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Fine. So Mr. Hennessy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just at this time, based on what was represented by the Prosecution in the last Status Conference that there were documents that were going to be produced that -- pursuant to their continuing responsibility under Rule 68, some documents have been produced, and I'd call upon the Court at this time to inquire whether we have everything that they conceive as being within their Rule 68 duties, or if not, when might we expect those things? That's my first issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: The Prosecution. Can the Prosecution address this point raised by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, the Prosecution does periodic comprehensive reviews of any new material that is coming into our possession every six months, on average every six months. In addition, if we become aware of any material that could be particularly relevant to the proceedings, we also review that material. At this point in time, we have concluded the last review around the end of October and disclosed anything that we found at that point in time. At that point in time, therefore, we are not aware of any further material that could fulfil the requirements of Rule 68. However, as I explained, we will continue to do our periodical reviews of new material that may come in our possession. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Hennessy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, Your Honour. As to another issue: We some time ago submitted documents for translation which we recovered, I see we, the Defence recovered since trial from the former Yugoslavia. Those documents I anticipate will be made part of a Rule 115 following -- filing, and I simply apprise the Court of our intent to do so. And my reason for informing the Court of this is that my concern is that here one day in the near future, I presume, oral arguments will be set on the appeal, and my first inquiry from the Prosecution, I just want to be sure that we have at least as far as they are aware everything that they conceive as being within Rule 68; on top of that, we have documents in translation that we've yet to receive in proper form for filing on a Rule 115 motion; and third, I inform the Court that I've just been notified that we have recovered additional documents in the former Yugoslavia that will have to be submitted for translation. So I would just raise it at this time in case the Court is attempting or considering scheduling oral arguments in the near future. I would ask that any such arguments be delayed until a ruling on any existing 115 motion or, as I've already said, the to-be-filed 115 motion. And I've just been reminded, Your Honour: There's also some documents that have been turned over to us by the Prosecution which are in translation as well, which I'm not sure yet whether they will be part of an additional filing. The documents were given to us, I believe, on August 29th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Hennessy, you know that according to the Rules, there are deadlines for filing motions under Article 115. Of course, if good cause is shown, these deadlines can be extended. So if -- are you referring to documents that have been disclosed by the Prosecution after the deadline had expired and you use them, of course you can make use of them. If it's other material, you have to show that you got -- that that material was available to you after the expiry of the deadline, because we cannot go on with the appeals forever. Now, if you are preparing a new 115 filing, first, please do it as quickly as possible. In your estimates, how much will that require? How long?

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Well, that's why I'm bringing it up, because we're here at a Status Conference, I'm giving you the status, and that is that we have not received them from translation. So at this point I'm waiting to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: When are you expecting to receive them from translation? What date were you given when you gave them for translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: I'm being told that the translation department says that we should have them sometime in January. That's all I've been told at present. But they've had these documents for some time already. I think two weeks, I'm being told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, I will not set you any specific deadline now, but I wanted only to -- that you are aware that when you submit a filing, you must give the reasons in the -- in your request why you come after the deadline which are specifically the reasons, in order that the Chamber may appreciate and justify the late filing or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Any other issue to be dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MR. KERNS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Kurt Kerns, if I may. I just wanted to make sure the record was clear with regard to these disclosure because if I understand what my colleague just said, the last status report August 29th mentions that they have received a bunch of documentation within the last three weeks prior to August 29th. They basically then go on to say we're going to give that to the Defence but we don't know when. At the end of the Status Conference last time, Your Honour ordered the Prosecution to basically provide us with a time line as to when that would be provided. If I hear my colleague correctly, I think what he said was we've completed that review from the August 29th disclosure and we did that in October, and right now we have everything. But if I misunderstood that representation, I'd like to know, because as far as I understand that representation, it is they have completed that review of the information mentioned in paragraph 7 of their status report and everything was given to us in October. Is that what they're saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution maybe clarify for the benefit of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The review of the material that has been mentioned during the last Status Conference on 28th August has been completed, and everything that the Prosecution found that could be Rule 68 has been provided to the Defence, to the appellants, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. Any other issue to be raised now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just for the record, we just received the English translation today, when we walked into court. And again, perhaps the Court could inquire as to the Office of the Prosecutor when they expect to have the approximately 16 documents that were in B/C/S only translated into English. That's the ones they handed us on the 29th of August. We still have not received them in English, and neither Mr. Hennessy nor I can read B/C/S. So until we read those, this is hampering us, obviously, Your Honour. If we believe that they are relevant Rule 115, we don't know that until we read them. And I still have not heard when we might have those translated. Only two were in English, I think approximately 16 were untranslated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution give any information on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Yes. We are expecting the outstanding translations to be completed roughly by the end of January. We have to note, however, that we were only informed by the appellant that they had problems with the B/C/S versions of the documents very recently, and since counsel for the appellant have to communicate with the appellant who -- which they presumably have to do in B/C/S, we did not -- we were not aware that there was a problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Very briefly. My colleagues, neither one of the colleagues here from the OTP were present on the 29th, but I want to inform the Court that I was informed that we would be getting the English translations, and so that's -- they're indicating we haven't talked to them, we didn't -- we talked to them on the 29th and we were informed that we would get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Just let me indicate, Your Honour: If that was the case, please accept our apologies. I wasn't on the case at the time, and we will certainly endeavour to get them to you as soon as possible, if that was the representation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Well, is there any other issue that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Mr. Hennessy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I forecast, the appellant Mr. Naletilic had asked to address the Court this afternoon, very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: It should be done very briefly. Please, Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT NALETILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to remind you: At the last Status Conference, we were speaking precisely about this same problem, and that is, the K56 proceedings in the Mostar court. It's obvious that none of you read those 30 statements which were provided to the Mostar court, and they are actually about precisely what I spoke about at the last sentence, and that is that I did not step into Sovici, and I had no command responsibility at all. Why am I saying this? Your Honour, during the proceedings, we did not have these 30 statements regarding Sovici and Doljani, nor did the Prosecution provide us, before the witnesses were questioned, but they gave us some of them after the -- all the Prosecution witnesses were questioned. So we were directly damaged or prejudiced in these proceedings. I really do not wish to take up too much of your time. I can see that we're all a little bit tense here. But I would just like to emphasise, Your Honour, that I have already been in prison for seven years, and I cannot think ill of the Prosecutor when they say it will come, it's going to come at the end of January, or we will give something, and something we will not. But again, I would like to ask you, Your Honour, if it's true that you did really intervene, because we really have received some of those documents. I don't know whether that was after your intervention or not. But I would like to ask you that the entire proceedings conducted in the Mostar court against the 26 persons, for the same acts that I have been convicted of here, I would like to have the whole case material from those cases here, and then we can look and see what we require and what we don't. In any of those statements, the Convicts' Battalion is never mentioned. Tutici is mentioned. The Convicts' Battalion is not mentioned here and it's not mentioned here, the persecution of the civilians, that I was convicted of here. There are names, there are the acts that they committed, but Tuta is not mentioned in any of those transcripts. So if we have the same rights as the Prosecution, I would request that you allow us that the Prosecutor from Mostar then hands over all those documents to us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, I listened to you, but, first, this Status Conference we cannot argue the merits of the case. And second, the arguments you are making should be made by your counsel. I mean, you have counsel, and counsel will raise these arguments in due course if they consider it appropriate. So it's difficult for me to take it from you without the assistance of your counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT NALETILIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one second. If you allow me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, I cannot go on in a private debate on these issues. I mean, I see your counsel remains silent, but probably they will raise the issue in due course when they deem it appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HENNESSY
utterances.text: And we intend to, Judge, and part of the delay and a source of Mr. Naletilic's aggravation, I'll call it, is delay in getting the documents translated, and once they're translated we will file something with the Court in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hennessy. Of course, I perfectly understand the feeling of the appellant, but I'm sure the Defence is taking care of his position. Any other matter? Mr. Farrell.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: This really isn't a matter of much concern, Your Honour, it's just that I think January 10th, which is the date on which the appellants are to file, I think that's a Saturday, so it may be better that it's noted as the 12th. If that's my understanding of the deadline that you set I think the 10th is a Saturday. That's all. Other than that, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Farrell. So let it be the 12th. You're correct, it's a Saturday, the 10th. I didn't think of it. So if there is no other matter to be raised now, we can adjourn. This Status Conference stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
